The test image shows a soybean stem/petiole with the distinctive signature of **Diaporthe**: black pycnidia (fruiting bodies) arranged in **linear rows** along the stem surface. This organized, linear alignment is the key diagnostic feature that differentiates Diaporthe from similar-looking diseases like Anthracnose (which has randomly scattered structures) and Charcoal Rot (which affects darkened tissue). The stem remains relatively green with dark structures on the surface, exactly matching the Diaporthe reference images and symptom description.
